title: To Blink or Not to Blink? A New Criterion to Quantify Luminescence Blinking
authors: Eduard A. Podshivaylov, Pavel A. Frantsuzov
abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots are promising materials for numerous applications due to their tunable emission and high quantum yields. However, emission instability in the form of luminescence blinking remains a significant obstacle to their practical implementation. While recent advances in synthesis and surface engineering have demonstrated partial or complete blinking suppression, the quantitative assessment of the "quality" of this suppression remains challenging. Existing criteria typically rely on threshold-based classification into ON and OFF states, which becomes inherently ambiguous owing to the continuous distribution of emission intensities in single quantum dots. Here, we propose a threshold-free two-dimensional quantitative criterion based on the variance of the recombination rate and the relative quantum yield, both of which can be extracted from standard time-correlated single-photon counting measurements. We validate the criterion using simulated blinking trajectories covering all major blinking mechanisms and demonstrate that it cleanly separates them into distinct regions of the two-dimensional parameter space while providing a quantitative measure of the degree of suppression. This approach directly quantifies the temporal stability of emission without requiring arbitrary state definitions, thereby providing a robust metric for comparing different blinking suppression strategies.
summary: The paper introduces a novel, threshold-free two-dimensional criterion based on the variance of recombination rate and relative quantum yield to quantify luminescence blinking in semiconductor quantum dots. By mapping different physical blinking mechanisms onto this parameter space, it offers a robust tool for assessing emission stability without relying on ambiguous ON/OFF state definitions.
main_problem: Luminescence blinking remains a major obstacle for colloidal quantum dots, and existing quantitative assessment methods based on arbitrary intensity thresholds are ambiguous.
main_result: The authors propose a robust, threshold-free two-dimensional criterion using the variance of the recombination rate and relative quantum yield to quantitatively classify different blinking mechanisms.
method: They derive and apply this 2D criterion $(\hat{\xi}, \langle\hat{Q}angle^{(s)})$ by analyzing time-correlated single-photon counting data, comparing it against simulations covering A-type, Trapping Mechanism (TM), and Hot Carrier (HC) blinking.
model_or_system: The system is colloidal semiconductor quantum dots exhibiting luminescence blinking. The analysis models the dynamics using instantaneous quantum yield $Y(t)$ and recombination rate $\Gamma(t)$, which are extracted from single-photon counting data.
key_observables: Variance of recombination rate ($\hat{\xi}$), self-consistent relative quantum yield ($\langle\hat{Q}angle^{(s)}$), ON/OFF time distributions, and the two-dimensional parameter space map.
important_parameters: The criterion distinguishes regimes: $\hat{\xi} \approx 1$ (constant rate), $\hat{\xi} = 0$ (two-state switching), and $(\hat{\xi} \approx 1, \langle\hat{Q}angle^{(s)} \approx 1)$ for complete suppression.
main_assumptions: The self-consistent estimator for quantum yield is preferred over naive estimators due to bias reduction; the analysis relies on extracting time-dependent rates from binned data.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the 2D blinking criterion diagram color-coding different mechanisms (Blue, White, Green, etc.). Other figures compare statistical diagnostics like ON/OFF distributions and Power Spectral Density for simulated TM blinking.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of existing threshold methods. It then introduces the two-dimensional $(\hat{\xi}, \langle\hat{Q}angle^{(s)})$ criterion, deriving the necessary estimators by comparing naive vs. self-consistent approaches. Finally, it validates this criterion by simulating and mapping known blinking mechanisms (A-type, TM, HC).
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative metric for characterizing open quantum systems dynamics (blinking) that moves beyond simple state counting, which is highly relevant to understanding decoherence and stability in solid-state emitters.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Two-dimensional blinking suppression criterion proposed in this work. The colored regions indicate characteristic areas corresponding to different lu- minescence blinking mechanisms. Blue (left): two-state blinking (A-type or two-state TM). White (center): sophisticated blinking: multilevel TM blinking and hybrid mechanisms. Green (right): hot-carrier (HC) blinking. Violet- pink (upper left): two-state ”stealth” blinking. Red (upper center): ”stealth” blinking- high relative quantum yield with persistent, non-two-state decay-rate fluctuations. Yellow-orange (upper right): complete non-blinking mode - the case of complete blinking suppression.

Figure 2: Simulated trajectories of (a) intensity and (b) lifetime for A-type blinking with corresponding distributions. (c) FLID extracted from the simu- lation. The solid red curve represents the theoretical ridge line. Note that the color scale is displayed on a logarithmic scale. Additionally, for contrast, points with fewer than 5 events have been removed. The simulation was run for up to 104 switching events with T + = T −= 30 ms and a bin size of 10 ms; only the first 30 s are shown.

Figure 3: TM blinking simulated using the model of Ref. 37. (a) Experimental blinking trace and photon-number distribution for a single CdSeS/ZnS quantum dot (QD 3.2 in Ref. 37); the red curve is the model fit. (b) Simulated trace and photon-number distribution generated with the parameters extracted from the fit; the red curve shows the theoretical expectation. (c) FLID extracted from the simulation, demonstrating the linear dependence characteristic of TM blinking. Simulation parameters and additional diagnostics are given in Supplementary Note 2.

Figure 4: Comparison of the naive and self-consistent estimators of the relative quantum yield. (a) A-type blinking with the OFF-state fraction pOFF varied from 0.1 to 0.9. Blue dashed curve: true theoretical quantum yield. Blue circles: mean of 10 simulations before Poisson noise (error bars: ±1 standard deviation). Red squares: self-consistent estimate ⟨ˆQ⟩(s). Black squares: naive estimate ⟨ˆQ⟩(0). (b) TM blinking with k0 varied over several orders of magnitude (parameters from QD 3.2 of Ref. 37). Symbols have the same meaning as in panel (a). Simulation parameters are listed in Supplementary Note 3.

Figure 5: Two-dimensional criterion (ˆξ, ⟨ˆQ⟩(s)) evaluated from simulations of A-type blinking (circles), TM blinking (upward triangles: QD 3.2; downward triangles: QD 4.4 from Ref. 37), and HC blinking (green squares). For A-type blinking, five values of kA/kr are used (0.1, 1, 5, 10, 20; see legend); for each, pOFF varies from 0.1 to 0.9. For TM blinking, k0 is varied at fixed α = 10 (red and green) and α is varied at fixed k0 (orange and cyan). Each point is the mean of 10 independent simulations. Simulation parameters are listed in Supplementary Note 3.
